suggestions.title: 1. MDMA: Magnesium Alarm, the first paragraph: what a tense jaw means, and what you have seen
suggestions.reading: The section read [AI Detected, 96%](https://www.pangram.com/history/08beb99e-4d7b-45b4-ac6f-32c9bfe3823a) on 2026-11-11, this paragraph in its first window, AI High.
suggestions.tested:
Try 1, your claim kept and the evidence said as what you've seen: "With MDMA, I treat meaningful jaw tension as the earliest warning that the body needs more magnesium. Nobody has tested this in a trial that I know of, so it's from what I've seen again and again: everyone I know who took enough magnesium chloride for the jaw tension to fully release avoided the other complications I've seen in people who let the tension keep going." [AI Generated](https://www.pangram.com/history/9e4a7d71-5ad6-4947-ad6f-b59269f9af9d): the first sentence AI Low, the rest AI High.

Try 2, the long sentence split and its mirror taken out: "... so it's from what I've seen myself. Everyone I know who took enough magnesium chloride for the jaw tension to fully release avoided the other complications that showed up when people let the tension keep going." [AI Generated](https://www.pangram.com/history/25bc9042-d058-40dd-b052-f7c2c6ab660f): AI Medium, then AI High.
suggestions.sense: Fresh readers asked what "meaningful" jaw tension is, when nearly everyone's jaw clenches on MDMA, and which "other complications" taking enough magnesium spared people. I couldn't answer either without putting words in your mouth.
suggestions.why: It is your claim and what you have seen, and the guide's fidelity check holds its words ("meaningful", "earliest", "warning"). How you'd say a claim from your own experience, with what it rests on, teaches me the guide's other paragraphs like it.
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: what a tense jaw on MDMA means, and what you've seen happen with and without enough magnesium, in your words. If you can say what "meaningful" tension looks like, or which complications you mean, that answers both readers.

suggestions.title: 2. MDMA: Magnesium Alarm, your second wife's story and what you took from it
suggestions.reading: The section read [AI Detected, 96%](https://www.pangram.com/history/08beb99e-4d7b-45b4-ac6f-32c9bfe3823a) on 2026-11-11, this paragraph AI-Assisted Low for the story and AI High for the lesson after it.
suggestions.tested:
Try 1: "What happened to my second wife is why I look past magnesium: she had severe convulsions after an MDMA overdose, and at the hospital they found her potassium critically low, described to me as essentially zero. IV potassium was the only treatment they gave her. So I treat serious MDMA toxicity as a broader electrolyte emergency, potassium included, even though magnesium is still the first and most useful intervention once the jaw tenses." [AI Generated](https://www.pangram.com/history/6840df55-84e4-4d02-9a14-086676b419a5): AI High, AI Medium, AI High.

Try 2, the story opening on itself and the short line joined to it: "My second wife had severe convulsions after an MDMA overdose, and at the hospital they found her potassium critically low, described to me as essentially zero, and IV potassium was the only treatment they gave her. So I treat ..." [AI Generated](https://www.pangram.com/history/162c5eaf-11c9-4eca-bdb6-e90cee404bc5): the story AI Medium, the lesson AI High.
suggestions.sense: A fresh reader said the paragraph opens a new story with nothing saying why it follows the magnesium talk, and that "a broader electrolyte emergency" doesn't say what to do differently. The lesson read AI High in every try, and the guide's fidelity check holds its words ("toxicity", "intervention", "broader"), so I can't say it plainer without your say.
suggestions.why: It is your story, and only you can tell it in your words. How you'd say what it taught you shows me how the guide's other lessons from your life should read.
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: what happened to her, and what it means for someone sitting with a friend on MDMA, in your words. Every fact of hers stays as you tell it; the words the fidelity check holds can change if you change them.
